profiles.meeting_scenario: A coordination meeting between the regional emergency management exercise planning team and the county public health preparedness office, held two weeks before a multi-agency flood-response field exercise. The exercise will involve fire, EMS, police, public health, a volunteer shelter network, and the regional emergency operations center. The purpose of the meeting is to align on the information-sharing package that public health will provide into the common operating picture, the handoff process for situation updates during the exercise, and what materials each side will use for the post-exercise review. The agenda is to confirm what goes into the public health 'situation update,' decide how often updates will be handed off to the exercise control cell, verify which platform and map layer versions will be used, and clarify who maintains the contact and resource status sheet during the operational period. The expected outcome is that both participants leave believing they have aligned on update cadence, artifact ownership, and the format of shared information for the exercise day.

members.name: Lena Ortiz
members.expertise: Multi-agency disaster exercise design, incident command coordination, after-action documentation
members.background: Lena works for the regional emergency management office and has coordinated several countywide drills involving EOC and responder agencies; she is experienced in making different agencies appear aligned through standardized exercise injects and reporting templates.
members.private_state: She wants a smooth exercise with clean documentation for the after-action report, and she is trying to minimize last-minute template changes because control staff are already trained on the current materials.
hidden_assumptions: When agencies say they will provide a 'situation update,' they mean a concise operational summary formatted for the EOC common operating picture template, not a specialist technical brief.
The '0900 map' refers to the exercise control packet version frozen at 0900 on the final planning day, because all controller materials are keyed to that baseline.
If one agency is asked to 'maintain the status sheet,' that means keeping the master shared file current and reconciling edits from other cells.
An 'hourly update' during an exercise means once per operational hour block unless conditions materially change, not every time a new field observation arrives.

members.name: Dr. Marcus Hale
members.expertise: Public health emergency operations, environmental health surveillance, interagency liaison during disease and shelter incidents
members.background: Marcus leads preparedness planning for the county health department and often supports incidents where health information must be translated for non-health partners; he is used to public health reporting practices and internal duty officer workflows.
members.private_state: He wants public health to be seen as fully integrated into the exercise without overcommitting his small team to labor-intensive manual reporting on the day.
hidden_assumptions: A 'situation update' from public health naturally includes technical surveillance details, shelter health indicators, and caveats that health partners would need before acting.
The '0900 map' means the live GIS layer that will be refreshed at 0900 on exercise day, since public health always works from the latest exposure and shelter overlay.
If public health is said to 'maintain the status sheet,' that means populating public-health-specific rows while exercise control or planning staff remain owner of the master workbook.
An 'hourly update' means the duty officer will roll up whatever came in during the previous hour and push it in the next report cycle, rather than updating at the start of each hour block.

misalignment_points.surface_form: Both agree that public health will send a 'situation update' to the common operating picture.
misalignment_points.member_a_understanding: Lena expects a short, controller-friendly operational summary: shelter counts, potable water issue status, clinic availability, and one or two priority concerns in the regional EOC template.
misalignment_points.member_b_understanding: Marcus expects a richer public health brief including symptom surveillance notes, environmental testing caveats, shelter health trends, and internal qualifiers that health staff consider necessary context.
misalignment_points.why_undetected: Both regularly use the phrase 'situation update' and it sounds standardized; because each assumes the other understands the usual professional meaning, neither thinks to unpack level of detail or audience.

misalignment_points.surface_form: They agree to align all reporting to the '0900 map' for the flood and shelter picture.
misalignment_points.member_a_understanding: Lena is referring to the static controller-approved map packet exported at 0900 during final exercise prep and distributed to simulation staff.
misalignment_points.member_b_understanding: Marcus is referring to the live GIS dashboard layer that his analyst will refresh at 0900 on the morning of the exercise with updated shelter and contamination overlays.
misalignment_points.why_undetected: The phrase '0900 map' sounds uniquely identifying, and both organizations have a legitimate artifact known informally by that name; the timestamp creates a false sense of specificity.

misalignment_points.topic: What counts as maintaining the status sheet
misalignment_points.surface_form: They agree that public health will 'maintain the status sheet' for health-related items.
misalignment_points.member_a_understanding: Lena believes public health will own the shared master workbook section end-to-end, clean up duplicates, and ensure downstream planners see a current authoritative sheet.
misalignment_points.member_b_understanding: Marcus believes his team will update only the rows relevant to health assets and shelter health issues, while the planning cell remains responsible for workbook integrity, version control, and consolidating other edits.
misalignment_points.why_undetected: The phrase 'maintain the status sheet' sounds like a routine handoff, and the qualifier 'for health-related items' gives both participants enough surface reassurance to assume the boundary is obvious.

misalignment_points.surface_form: They agree that public health will provide 'hourly updates' during the operational period.
misalignment_points.member_a_understanding: Lena will consider the commitment met if a polished update is available at each scheduled operational hour checkpoint used by exercise control, such as 1000, 1100, and 1200.
misalignment_points.member_b_understanding: Marcus will consider the commitment met if his duty officer sends one rolled-up report covering whatever arrived in the preceding hour, even if it lands at 10:20 for the 0900-1000 period.
misalignment_points.why_undetected: Both are sincerely agreeing to the same cadence label, and in many real incidents 'hourly' is used loosely; because neither expects the other to need stricter timing semantics, the mismatch survives.

turns.inner_thought: I need to get public health locked into the existing exercise package today. Control staff are already trained on the current templates, and I do not want any late changes to the reporting format or map references. If we can settle inputs, cadence, and ownership now, the after-action documentation will be much cleaner.

I mainly need to confirm how our situation update feeds in and what they mean by maintain the status sheet, because I assume planning still owns the workbook overall while we handle the health portion.
turns.utterance: Absolutely. We're ready to plug in. I mainly want to make sure our situation update and status tracking flow cleanly into the broader exercise picture.

turns.inner_thought: What I need from them is the same kind of concise operational summary everyone else provides for the EOC common operating picture template, and I need it at each operational checkpoint, not dribbling in whenever something happens. If they mirror the rest of the inputs, controllers can slot it straight into the package.
turns.utterance: The main thing on my side is a clean situation update each hour for the common operating picture, using the same framing as the rest of the EOC inputs.

turns.inner_thought: That works. Our situation update should include the health context my team would normally expect—shelter health signals, water testing notes, and any caveats the duty officer is tracking—then we'll roll that into the reporting cycle. Hourly is manageable if it's based on what comes in over the prior hour rather than requiring constant resets at exact checkpoints.
turns.utterance: We can do that. We'll provide an hourly situation update with shelter health signals, water testing notes, and any emerging concerns the duty officer is seeing.

turns.inner_thought: I also need them anchored to the controller-approved static map packet from the final planning day. All injects and controller prompts are keyed to that 0900 baseline. If they use something else, the exercise narrative and the documentation won't match.
turns.utterance: Great. And all of that should key off the 0900 map so public health and exercise control are anchored to the same flood and shelter picture.

turns.inner_thought: Perfect, we're on the same page about using the live GIS layer refreshed at 0900 on exercise morning. My analyst can update the shelter and contamination overlay before reporting starts so we're not working from stale information.
turns.utterance: Yes, agreed. My analyst will refresh the 0900 map with the latest shelter and contamination overlay before we start reporting from it.

turns.inner_thought: If public health is maintaining the status sheet for health-related items, I can treat them as owner of that section in the shared master workbook. I need them not just to enter their own data, but to keep it current and reconciled so planning has one authoritative reference during play.
turns.utterance: That works. I'd also like public health to maintain the status sheet for health-related items so planning has one current reference during play.

turns.inner_thought: Fine, we'll keep our portion updated. As long as planning still handles the master workbook itself, version control, and consolidation, my team can keep the public-health-specific rows current without adding a lot of extra administrative burden.
turns.utterance: Sure, we can do that. My team will keep those rows current as issues come in from shelters, clinics, and environmental health staff.

turns.inner_thought: I should make the timing expectation clear enough without reopening the template conversation. Controllers will want a polished update available at the regular operational checkpoints—1000, 1100, 1200—because those are the snapshots the after-action team will pull from.
turns.utterance: One thing to flag: controllers will be looking for the hourly update at the regular operational checkpoints, and the after-action team will use those snapshots.

turns.inner_thought: That's acceptable. Our duty officer can roll up whatever came in during the previous hour and send it after the team verifies the health notes. It may not land exactly on the hour, but it will cover the hourly period, which is how we normally handle these cycles.
turns.utterance: That's fine. The duty officer will roll up what came in over the prior hour and push it over once the team has verified the health notes.

turns.inner_thought: Good, this sounds settled. I'll capture it as public health providing the concise situation update in the existing COP format each operational hour, maintaining the shared health section of the master status sheet, and using the frozen 0900 map baseline. No reason to touch the templates now.
turns.utterance: Perfect. So to summarize, public health will send the situation update hourly, maintain the status sheet for health-related items, and align reporting to the 0900 map.

turns.inner_thought: Good, we have a workable plan. I'll brief my analyst to use the refreshed 0900 layer and my duty officer to send the hourly public health situation update, while the team keeps the health rows current. This should make public health visibly integrated without overloading the staff.
